signals.evidence: Host describes persistent threat awareness: 'When you put your head on the pillow, you still hear the sound of alarm sirens even when they're not there'
Host reports: 'Recently there have been many displaced persons and evacuations...shelters aren't really providing protection for citizens'

Host describes uncertainty about ceasefire implications: 'After this grace period of the ceasefire agreement ends—what next? What will we do? How does it affect your daily plans? What about schools, planes, travel, projects?'
Caller Salim expresses deep anxiety about conflict's religious dimensions and fear that missiles will target Al-Aqsa mosque
Caller Salim reports: 'schools are closed'
Caller Salim describes economic pressure: 'Most people are debt-burdened with mortgages, loans, and car payments, and must work constantly just to survive monthly expenses'
Host summarizes social paralysis: 'We're just waiting like a herd being led toward unknown destination, aware of uncertainty but without agency or information to plan ahead'
Caller Majed reports: 'Families evacuated young children from the area and children have become traumatized by the violence'
Caller Majed describes: 'The war is affecting people's psychology a lot, especially children and schools. Children's dog refused toys because they were so distressed'
Caller Majed states: 'We are trying to adapt to these matters' and expresses hope for permanent ceasefire but willingness to find alternative survival strategies
Caller Durayd proposes: 'Any newly built mosque should be designed so that it has a legitimate shelter' because mosques were threatened with closure during wartime

Caller Muhammad reports: 'I prayed all the Taraweeh prayers in a garage for five years while mosques were being built' and 'Many women stayed home because worship at home is not the same as in the mosque'
Female shopkeeper describes Old City during war: 'You'd see cars everywhere, old things, like a ghost town...The Old City was closed—doors locked, shops closed, no people'
Female shopkeeper reports: 'I owe 3,000 shekels in monthly rent for my shop, which I could not pay during the entire war period because I had no income'
Female shopkeeper describes landlord-tenant conflict: 'The shop owner tells you: my source of income is the rent from this shop...so he has the right to collect the rent'
Military correspondent reports ongoing rocket fire from Lebanon into northern Israel and Galilee; some rockets fell in open areas with no reported casualties or damage
Shin Bet and Israeli Police announce arrest of 22-year-old Haifa resident who manufactured explosive materials intended to harm senior figures for Iranian intelligence operatives
Education Minister announced school holiday program extension without Finance Ministry input; Finance Ministry clarifies program lacks their agreement and has no allocated budget
Host critiques military narrative: 'When Hezbollah continues to bombard the north with missiles, it is again proven that residents on the border remain exposed to an enemy that was not destroyed'
Host announces renewed rocket alerts in northern region and urges listeners to follow Civil Defense directives
First Sergeant Tuvul Yosef Lipshitz killed during operations against terrorist cell in southern Lebanon; five other soldiers wounded in the incident
Fallen soldier's family agreed to donate his organs to save lives
Mentor describes fallen soldier: 'He was the first to volunteer in every training exercise, always gave everything he had'
Youth leader describes Tobal: 'He was a boy with tremendous modesty who didn't tell anyone about anything; he did things in secret'
Youth leader recounts: 'He showed up unannounced at an intensive winter training and just was there, telling the soldiers I see you, I'm here for you'
Youth leader describes: 'We see families that had every reason to break, but they chose differently—they draw strength and share it'
Emergency broadcast directs civilians in northern border communities to immediately enter protected spaces and follow Home Front Command instructions
Rambam Hospital managing approximately 1,100 patients total with 910 still hospitalized, operating from underground bunker facilities for protection
Rambam Hospital functioning as major trauma center for soldiers wounded in Lebanon, maintaining readiness for potential surge capacity while operating underground
Rambam trauma center treats blast wounds, fragmentation injuries, and limb trauma from current operations; some soldiers requiring amputation; civilian casualty in critical condition in ICU

Hospital staff organized music and celebration event in underground facility to lift morale; administrator emphasizes: 'Even underground they're trying to experience, to trust, to enjoy, to feel hope, to embrace one another'
Northern council leader expresses concern: 'Residents in the Upper Galilee are in shelters constantly—in Kiryat Shmona, Kfar Giladi, Metula, Moshav, Manara—all the time in that space'

Northern council leader criticizes: 'What concerns residents right now is really who is making the decisions, and if ultimately decisions come from the United States, the results of this war could be very hard for us'
Northern council leader calls for government investment: 'If the Israeli government knows there's a whole region left in war, it should open its coffers and say, prepare better plans'

Northern leader critiques disparity: 'When you hear that the State of Israel is returning—educational institutions, cultural institutions in Israel are returning to work—it's as if two states exist...The peripheral region that has been neglected for years'
Northern leader states: 'This is an expression of the fact that people are currently becoming second-class citizens in the state, even during this war'
Council leader affirms: 'The residents of the Upper Galilee choose to live in the Upper Galilee every day. They love the place, and even during this war, they chose to stay'
Council leader expresses optimism: 'I say in the end our residents will continue to live here...we're confident we'll succeed in settling and rebuilding—but it won't be simple'

Mayor Avihai Stern: 'We heard the whole world talking about a ceasefire unifying arenas that includes everyone, and we heard the opposite from our prime minister in a statement saying a ceasefire does not include Lebanon. This created confusion.'
Sustained barrage of rocket fire from Lebanon targeting northern Israel; multiple rockets intercepted while others fell in open and agricultural areas.

School reopening amid ongoing security situation with some students returned, others not returned, and still others unable to return due to security constraints; schools previously served as public shelters.

Education correspondent Lior Wortslewski: Northern and Golan region students remain largely displaced; Haifa and surrounding areas designated as closed regions where learning only occurs in protected spaces, meaning learning remains extremely limited.

Many municipalities proactively opened schools before official authorizations, with varying start times and meal/hour configurations, recognizing psychological necessity and practical importance for children and parents.
Municipalities independently opened schools with varying operational models (different start times, meal provision, hours) before receiving official authorization, demonstrating local initiative.
Education correspondent: Expanded summer school program estimated at 750 million shekels; Education Ministry stated there is currently no funding available for this expansion.
Teacher: 'Children who were home a lot, facing screens, accumulated problems—they are tense, they jump at sounds, some have no home to return to, their home was damaged and they were evacuated.'
Parents expressed great joy at sending children to school to be in care of educators who have been working and coping for 40 days, indicating reliance on institutional support for child wellbeing.
Golan regional council chairman: 'We came to over 80% of children arriving at educational institutions, kindergartens, schools, certainly high schools in southern Golan—we have very good compliance.'
Golan regional council chairman: 'We've built over 50 shelters in eight months in the Golan regional council.'

Golan regional council chairman: 'The good things are that the Golan, despite a year and a half of war, has not left the communities for a moment and maintains constant resilience and as much routine as possible.'

Golan council leader: Kindergarten hours cut from 4 to 2 PM with delayed opening times due to insufficient staffing from educators unable to reach posts from restricted areas and transportation challenges.
Golan council leader: 'Almost all kindergarten teachers volunteered over the past month and a half and were full partners in what we're doing.'
Resource center director: Over 250 new treatment requests for children in past month; widespread behavioral regression, nocturnal enuresis, and severe anxiety among children aged 5 to teenagers.
Mental health professional: 'Children ages 5 and 8 are returning home at night due to fear of going to the bathroom alone—this is part of what we handle in resilience centers in the north.'
Resource center: 115 requests for focused parental guidance and over 250 new referrals for treatment of children ages 0-13 in past 1.5 months.
Mental health professional: 'Parents take children to parks, they hear words like ceasefire and relaxation, but in reality they hear explosions and sirens—how do we rebuild that trust?'

Mental health professional Alon Abnet: 'Children who completed successful therapy are calling back saying they need help again—they wake crying at night, startle at every sound, and ask parents to accompany them to the bathroom.'
Previously discharged child clients are re-engaging treatment; mental health center simultaneously managing new pediatric cases, indicating both relapse of treated trauma and acute new trauma.
Volunteers and soldiers prepared festivities in protected spaces at military bases, demonstrating adaptive community resilience in maintaining holiday observance despite security tensions.
Football stadiums remain closed in northern regions due to ongoing conflict; military command restrictions on gathering limits prevent stadium reopening.
Sports correspondent: 'Rockets landing in the middle of the football pitch in Kiryat Shmona, that same pitch always so familiar, so mythological that always calmed us.'
Sports correspondent: 'During a football match, all the players, although on the pitch, they all go down, evacuate to protected spaces.'
